Bring an old book, leave with a new one.              Libraries are a place for community, culture, and activism. The West End Branch of the Boston Public Library is no exception. Join us for the opening of a new special exhibit tracing the history of the neighborhood library and its impact.    Originally opening in 1896 in the Old West Church, the branch saw decades of change as the West End gained a vibrant immigrant community and eventually faced the wrecking ball of urban renewal. The West End Branch became the cradle of memories of the Old West End as host for the collections that would give rise to the West End Museum.    It wouldn’t be a library event if you didn’t leave with a book! Take a book and leave a book for The WEM’s second Free to All Book Swap. Bring gently used books to share with neighbors and exchange them with old friends and new.    Admission is free, but bringing books is encouraged!    Light refreshments will be available. events.title: The Space Consortium's Space Table
events.description:
Whether you're a space professional, student, educator, science communicator, longtime space enthusiast, or simply curious about space, come enjoy an informal evening of conversation, games, and new connections.

The Space Table is our new monthly gathering bringing together Space Consortium Members (MA-based space academics and professionals) and Explorers (space enthusiasts) for space and science conversations, board games, discussions, and more. What happens at The Space Table will be shaped by you: share what you're working on, pick a space or science topic to discuss, join a game, meet someone with completely different expertise, and tell us what you'd like to see at future gatherings.

No space background or expertise is required. Everyone is welcome!
Free and open to all: Registration is free, but spots are limited, so register now to reserve yours.

events.title: Jesse Gallagher  + Steve Fell
events.description:
$10 admission / 7pm / seated show Jesse Gallagher  began living above the Lilypad in 2006, just a few blocks from where his grandfather grew up on Inman st.  At the time Jesse was in the middle of what would be about a decade of regular touring, performing & recording with his psychedelic rock band Apollo Sunshine.  The band was featured in the New York Times, Rolling Stone, Spin & shared the stage with legendary acts  Wu-Tang Clan ,  Toots & The Maytals ,  The Flaming Lips  &  Dr. Dog . Jesse has been involved with the Lilypad for 20 years and the full time talent booking agent since 2013. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Breaking Bad used Jesse’s song “We are Born When We Die” (2008) to dramatic effect. “Today is the Day” (2005) was in international Nike commercials while his “Singing to the Earth to Thank Her For You” was used in a large GAP campaign. Gallagher has collaborated, recorded & performed extensively w/  Sam Cohen ,  Willy Mason ,  Lilys ,  Nick Nicely ,  Doug Tuttle  &  Edan . Gallagher is a certified Yoga & Meditation teacher and hosts classes at the Lilypad & online. Since 2018, he has released 40 pieces of instrumental music which have been used in millions of YouTube videos ranging from NBC NY to Tesla and most recently a string of viral videos by Emma Chamberlain. Gallagher has a very active YouTube channel, making lots of psychedelic music videos and building a community of mindful listeners. @jessegallagher.tv Steve Fell  is a guitarist, composer, and educator whose performing and recording career over the last twenty five years has reached across the boundaries of jazz, experimental, funk, free form improvisation, rock, electronic, reggae/calypso, hip-hop, psych, and many others.   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 He co-leads the groups  Clear Audience, Quantum Banditos, Dome Room,  and  Astronomico,  leads a trio under his own name, and collaborates with numerous bands and artists. @stevefellmusic

events.description:
$10 advance / $12 at the door / 10:30 doors / 10:45 show / standing 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Midnight Confessions  is a singer-songwriter night showcasing three talented up-and-coming artists. Join us for a night of community, great music, and confessions at midnight. 
 
 
 
 Double-click to edit... 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Kiera Reale 
 
 
 Kiera Reale is a singer/songwriter known for her blend between emotionally resonant folk/pop tracks and cinematic, orchestral arrangements. Her songs talk about a variety of different topics from mental health struggles, hope, and the human experience. She writes, records, and produces all of her own tracks, and is currently working on new music following the release of her debut EP,  Everything I Say Haunts Me. linktr.ee/kierareale 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Ella Loretta 
 
 
 Ella Loretta is a singer, songwriter, and actress from Raleigh, North Carolina, known for inventive melodies, addictive hooks, and emotion-driven storytelling. Her powerful, expressive voice and lyrical dexterity make her songs "instantly memorable" (Vents Magazine). Ella creates pop music for the passionate. She has worked with Grammy Award winning producer Matt Rollings and collaborated in Los Angeles with Hardcover, the recording studio and company of Harold Lilly, Grammy Award winning songwriter and music executive. In 2024 she won the Athena Prize Festival Songwriting Competition in Nashville Tennessee. Most recently, Ella's single Really Do won Best Original Song at the 2026 Hollywood Independent Music Awards. linktr.ee/ellaloretta 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Lauren Kusiciel  
 
 
 Lauren Kusiciel is a pop-rock artist from the Chicagoland area. Her dreamy pop lyrics combined with grunge-inspired rock guitars and vocals blend together to create something truly unique and yet, familiar. Lauren isn’t afraid to tell the hard truths. Her emotion comes through with every word. Lauren is currently building her repertoire, Creating something new every day.  linktr.ee/laurenkusiciel

events.description:
$20-$25 at the door / $15 students & seniors / 11:45 doors / 12pm start  Experience the magic of a moving meditation with Integral Yoga instructor Vienna-Parashakti. This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. (cash or venmo accepted at the door) Class will be cancelled Nov. 28th. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Parashakti  (Vienna) is an Integral Yoga instructor and Somerville resident. Since 2022, she spent two and a half years studying and teaching Hatha at  Satchidananda Ashram  in Yogaville, Virginia before moving to Massachusetts.  She is currently teaching weekly Integral Yoga Hatha classes at the Lilypad and other spaces around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yoga Classes at Lilypad continue weekly on Saturdays.

events.description: Toad Revival Series — Saturdays, 4–7 PM  Every Saturday from 4 to 7, we rewind the clock and let the old sparks fly. The  Toad Revival Series  is our tribute to the bands that built this stage, note by note, night after night. It’s a laid-back, early evening show filled with familiar sounds, longtime favorites, and the spirit of a scene that never really faded—just waited for the right time to plug back in. These are the artists who gave Toad its heartbeat, returning for intimate, no-frills sets that remind us why we’re here. Think front-porch energy with barroom volume, old songs with new life, and a crowd that knows when to sing along. Come early. Stay as long as you like. This is Toad, the way it was—and still is.

In keeping with the international flavour of our imaginary café, the diversity of styles ranges from traditional/contemporary Classical and Film music to innovative jazz fusions, experimental, and dance-hall music.

 Boston-based saxophone quartet Jade Quartet was the winner of the Boston University Chamber Music Competition in 2025. The ensemble’s members, professional musicians who also serve as educators in various music institutions in Boston, have performed at renowned venues such as Symphony Hall and Jordan Hall in Boston, as well as Carnegie Hall in New York. Bringing together their distinctive musical backgrounds and artistry, Jade Quartet is actively engaged in performances throughout Massachusetts and in collaborations with composers. Having pursued their studies and professional activities across France, Spain, and the United States, each member brings a unique musical voice and perspective to the ensemble. Together, their diverse backgrounds and individual styles shape Jade Quartet’s distinctive musical identity and continue to inspire their work on stage.

 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang.  A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. events.description:
$15 admission / $10 students / 7pm  / seated 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang. As co-leader of Earprint, he received critical acclaim from publications such as Downbeat magazine, NPR’s critics' poll and many more.  www.dorherskovits.com

events.description:
$15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated  Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Plamen Karadonev,  Piano Sean Farias,  Bass Special Guest , Trumpet 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Double-click to edit... 
 
 
 
 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

 The Fringe  originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist  George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. events.title: TCS presents: Gary Gulman (A Benefit for The Malaria Consortium)
events.description:
18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum. Doors at 630pm / Show at 730pm. Please Arrive Early to Guarantee Seating.
Gary Gulman
 has made five masterful TV specials, including his most recent universally acclaimed stand-up specials for HBO Max, “Born On 3rd Base”, lending his meticulous comedic craft to the current Tale of Two Cities-esque wealth gap, and “The Great Depresh”, a tour de force look at mental illness, which is equal parts hilarious and inspiring. Most recently, Gary made his off-Broadway debut with a 5-week sold-out run at The Lucille Lortel Theatre of his critically acclaimed one-man show “Grandiloquent,” directed by Tony Award winner Moritz von Stuelpnagel and produced by Mike & Carlee Productions (“Oh Mary”). Today, Gulman is one of the most popular touring comics, selling out theaters around the country including the prestigious Carnegie Hall in New York City. Gary is currently touring with “Misfit: A Gary Gulman Stand Up & Book Tour”, which features material based on his book, but not a repeat of the book. Gary lives in Harlem with his wife.
The Malaria Consortium
 is an organisation of global health and malaria specialists creating tangible, scalable and sustainable impact. As a global health charity with 20 years of proven impact against malaria, we are uniquely positioned to unite key partners in achieving a world free of malaria, where equitable access to healthcare empowers people and enables communities to thrive. Why partner with us? Our deep, on-the-ground, technical expertise, unique focus on implementation science, powerful partnerships and an ability to scale interventions cost-effectively — all backed by reliable governance.

 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. She is currently teaching weekly Integral Yoga Hatha classes at the Lilypad and other spaces around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound."

I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ”

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - Tim Gearan Band
events.description: A beloved fixture in the Boston music scene for over 25 years, Tim Gearan has become a bonafide local music hero. His warm, raspy baritone, jaw-dropping guitar skills and wry, poignant songwriting have graced the bars, pubs, and music halls throughout New England and beyond, creating a loyal cult-like following. Gearan, a New York native, spent ten years touring the globe as a sideman for the great Toni Lynn Washington, as well as collaborating with Grammy-winning singer/guitarist Susan Tedeschi. Finding his own artistic voice, Gearan  has crafted an intoxicating blend of Americana, folk and blues with shades of Randy Newman, Tom Waits, JJ Cale,  Leon Russell and Lowell George. He quickly established himself as a force in the Boston’s resurgent roots music scene, and his Boston area residencies have become a “can’t miss” staple of the city’s nightlife. Gearan has released 7 albums to date, as well as 4 single releases; “While the World Goes By” (2019)  “It’s Not the End of the World"  (2019) “Hey, Hey, Hey” (2020) and “Talk About Heaven” (2020).

events.title: Eliza Edens & Nora Meier
events.description:
$12 advance / $15 day of show / 9:15 doors / 9:30 music / all ages Brooklyn-based songwriter Eliza Edens celebrates the release of their latest record 'Death Drive.' Local songwriter Nora Meier supports. 
 
 
 
 
    RSVP
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Eliza Edens  is a Brooklyn-based songwriter who writes songs that dance inside the white-hot intersection of pleasure and pain. Bold and sincere, their songs are like antique cameo necklaces–snapshots of tenderness, worn close to the heart. A palette of punchy electric guitars and drums, gentle keys, and flourishes of saxophone and electronic percussion accent Edens’ voice as they sing of lovers & lilacs, grief & gratitude, and Freud’s “death drive.” Chameleonic in nature, Edens touches corners of pop, rock, folk, and country–with their voice as the glue that binds each genre foray together into a commanding sound. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Edens came up initially on the DIY songwriter circuit–playing self-booked tours of small clubs and listening rooms on the quiet success of 2020’s  Time Away From Time  and 2022’s lush acoustic-fingerpicked  We’ll Become the Flowers . They earned praise from outlets such as Paste Magazine, The Nashville Scene, Spill Magazine, and Americana UK while incessantly touring across America. Cutting their teeth on the road eventually paid off as Edens won runner-up at the esteemed Telluride Troubadour Songwriting competition in 2024. The veneer of a quiet songster singing breezy Nick Drake-esque melodies was quickly dashed after Edens lost their mother in late 2024 after a long journey with early-onset dementia. After releasing 2025’s lo-fi collection of voice memos  it’s your birthday & you’re gorgeous  with no fanfare or promotion, Edens disappeared from touring for the better part of a year. Some say Edens went out to New Mexico to find god. Others say Edens turned into a butterfly and floated south to greener pastures. Edens will say that they continued to find hope in writing songs. Newly molded by the black hole of grief, the singer reemerges this fall with their first record in 4 years.  Death Drive  is the sound of someone finding themself while also losing control. Heavy and light, black and neon-tinged, the album is a masterful achievement of contemporary indie rock, poignantly moving through the landscape of grief while also foisting joy, love, and humor up to the light. Website  |  Bandcamp  |  Facebook  |  Instagram  |  TikTok  |  Twitter  |  YouTube  |  Spotify 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Nora Meier  (she/her) is a diehard music fan, a frequent moviegoer, a daughter of two English majors, an Oregonian at heart, a verbal processor, a big reader, extremely stubborn, and always writing. What Spectrum Culture calls her "Old World sense of wear and wonder" (Velucci) finds balance in a fresh realism born from a deep attention to the details of everyday living. Her songwriting is an invitation to take a clear-eyed look at ourselves and the world around us with a healthy dose of humor and warmth.  	Meier’s first release since her 2024 debut album,  Outfield , marks a departure from softer sounds towards a wilder, more confident and embodied expression of her lyricism. “Bird in the Hand” is inspired by her love of alt-country singer-songwriters like Jeff Tweedy and Lucinda Williams, whose words live at the forefront of their arrangements and shine against a lush textural backdrop. “Bird in the Hand” starts out like a straightforward love song, but by the time it crescendoes into the bridge and Meier sings, “ for the first time I feel it / that I could fall and land”  the lines blur between the romance of a potential relationship and the romance of manifesting personal dreams. “Bird in the Hand” is an affirmation that some risks are worth taking. The single was produced and mixed by Don Mitchell (Darlingside) and mastered by Andrew Goldring (Olivia Barton, Abigayle Oakley). It was released on May 29th, 2026.  Website  l  Facebook  I  Instagram  I  Bandcamp  l  YouTube

events.description:
$15 admission / $10 students / 7pm  / seated 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang. As co-leader of Earprint, he received critical acclaim from publications such as Downbeat magazine, NPR’s critics' poll and many more.  www.dorherskovits.com

events.description:
$15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated  Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Plamen Karadonev,  Piano Sean Farias,  Bass Special Guest , Trumpet

 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

 The Fringe  originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist  George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. events.description:

This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. (cash or venmo accepted at the door) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Parashakti  (Vienna) is an Integral Yoga instructor and Somerville resident. Since 2022, she spent two and a half years studying and teaching Hatha at  Satchidananda Ashram  in Yogaville, Virginia before moving to Massachusetts.  She is currently teaching weekly Integral Yoga Hatha classes at the Lilypad and other spaces around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yoga Classes at Lilypad continue weekly on Saturdays.

events.title: Molecular
events.description:
$10 at the door / 5pm doors / 5:30 show / seated & standing / all ages Free admission for the first 36 reservations at  www.elarmusic.com/molecular In the quiet isolation of the laboratory, amid the hum of vacuum pumps and the irritability of failed reactions, I found stories hidden in the molecules.  Molecular  is the culmination of those long nights: the frustration of broken bonds, the sudden spark of an unexpected synthesis, and the realization that the atomic world mirrors the depth of our own emotions. Each piece narrates a concept rooted in the molecular world, exploring matter through the raw vulnerability of the human condition. Join ELAR for an evening of original compositions for piano and voice. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 ELAR 
 
 
 ELAR  is a Venezuelan composer and pianist who has been writing music for more than 20 years. Based in Inman Square, he is an independent artist driven by a love of composition, and he draws inspiration from the people closest to him, philosophical ideas, and the life sciences. He is also a chemist, and his music is where two seemingly immiscible worlds mix. In ELAR’s hands, a broken bond, a failed reaction, or a sudden spark of discovery becomes melody and harmony. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 www.elarmusic.com/molecular  | Instagram: @elarmusic |  Spotify

events.description:
free admission! / 1pm doors / seated & standing Celebrate Nicholas Brust on his birthday with a jazz showcase at the Lilypad. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Wielding a unique, incisive and soulful voice as an improviser and composer, Boston-based jazz saxophonist Nicholas Brust (pronounced “Bruhst”) has established his voice in the world of modern improvised music. Nicholas has found his niche as a bandleader and sideman, taking advantage of the numerous textures and combinations available in the traditional jazz small-group format. Brust has performed and/or recorded with numerous highly acclaimed musicians, including Lage Lund, Gilad Hekselman (with bassist Jon Latona), Mark Ferber (with pianist Francesca Prihasti), The Peter Silver Big Band (sharing the stage with Roy Hargrove, Jimmy Owens, Steve Wilson and others), guitarist Ben Eunson, Kristina Koller (appearing in her Quintet at the 2020 NYC Winter Jazz Fest), and many others. Nicholas is currently on faculty at New England Conservatory as part of its Prep/Continuing Education division in addition to being an Artslink Teaching Artist for Berklee College of Music’s City Music program. Having released 2 albums as a leader, Nicholas recently recorded a third that he plans to release in March 2027.

events.description:
$15 admission / $10 students / 7pm  / seated 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang. As co-leader of Earprint, he received critical acclaim from publications such as Downbeat magazine, NPR’s critics' poll and many more.  www.dorherskovits.com

 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

 Joe Hunt  is a jazz drummer, educator, author, and historian. In the early 1960s, Joe Hunt performed and recorded alongside the late NEC Distinguished Artist-in-Residence Emeritus George Russell, with releases on Decca and Riverside. Hunt joined The Stan Getz Quartet in 1964, recording several releases on Verve, then was a member of the Bill Evans Trio from 1966-1967. The remainder of the 1960s found Hunt performing or recording with several other jazz luminaries including Chet Baker, Eric Dolphy, Dizzy Gillespie, Dexter Gordon, Charles Mingus, Bob Brookmeyer, and the late Herb Pomeroy. In the 1970s and 1980s, Hunt was a member of The National Jazz Ensemble, led jazz groups with John Scofield, Mike Stern, and Santi Debriano, and toured with quartets of Red Rodney and Hal McKusick. The 1990s, and beyond, have included membership in The Smithsonian Jazz Masters Orchestra, with former NEC president Gunther Schuller, performances with Kenny Burrell, Joe Lavano, Joanne Brackeen, and Tal Farlow, as well as recordings with the Bert Seager Quintet, and also, Trio. Hunt is the author of the 1994 book 52nd Street Beat, which is a historical look at jazz drummer greats from 1945 to 1965. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Joe Hunt quartet features a modern jazz ensemble music played by top local pros: Mark Pinto - alto saxophone, formerly years with the Buddy Rich band John Lockwood – bass, formerly with Joe Henderson, Lee Konitz, current Fringe member Yuka Hamano Hunt – piano, voice, arranger Joe Hunt – drums, formerly with George Russell, Stan Getz, Jim Hall, Dexter Gordon, and Bill Evans We pay tribute to a special composer or performer at most performances. Recent shows have included: Burt Bacharach, Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Gigi Gryce. Future shows will include the music of Paul and Carla Bley, and arranger, Johnny Mandel. - Continuing of the 3rd Sunday of Every Month

 Fredy Guzmán is a Peruvian guitarist, composer, and arranger known for blending the musical traditions of the Andes with jazz, blues, and contemporary rock. A graduate of Berklee College of Music, he is the creator of  Waijazz , a musical project that bridges Andean heritage, Quechua culture, and modern improvisation. His albums include  Waijazz  (2015),  ¡Ay Vida!  (2019), and  Room to Be  (2024), reflecting his ongoing exploration of Peruvian identity through music. Performing internationally, Fredy continues to share the sounds and spirit of the Andes with audiences around the world. www.fredyguzman.com

events.title: Untidy 20th Anniversary Show feat. Hallway
events.description:
$15 admission / 5:15 doors / 5:30 start / seated & standing / all ages 
 
 
 
 
    get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 On New Year’s Eve 2006, high-school freshmen Ryan, Matty, and Josh played a six-song set for their friends, marking the beginning of the band now known as  Untidy .  Celebrating the 20th anniversary of their first ever show, Untidy is thrilled to be joined by Hallway, another product of Sharon, MA, and an emerging talent on the Boston indie scene. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Untidy 
 
 
 Untidy is a Boston-based power trio formed in 2006 by childhood friends Ryan, Josh, and Matty. They quickly developed a signature indie rock sound built around vocal harmonies and driving rhythms. By 2010, a relentless focus on songwriting and recording propelled them to two wins at their high school’s battle of the bands, a trip to the NAMM show in Anaheim, CA, and their debut album  One Small Step for Man  under the moniker High Tide. Leaving home for college offered not only opportunities for growth—including a sophomore album  Soft Shoulders  as Pons—but also diverging interests. A hiatus followed graduation, and eventually all three moved out of state.   Post-pandemic returns to Massachusetts reunited the friends and reignited their songwriting chemistry. They reintroduced themselves as Untidy in January 2025 with the release of their comeback album  Where Have You Been? , chronicling lessons learned in their decade apart. That momentum has carried into 2026, with a return to live performances and the release of singles “Turn the Corner,” “Evensong,” and “Need.” A fourth album is due for release in early 2027. @untidyband Untidy on  Spotify 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Hallway 
 
 
 All from south of Boston, the members of Hallway all met in school, where their love of music connected them, yet they would not form together until after they had all graduated. While attending college on different sides of New England, the group has been writing and performing. During the breaks and Summer of their first year together, the group has been able to create an energetic and vibrant music scene in the surrounding area of their hometown. Additionally, their fanbase is growing and strong. Hallway’s nostalgic and powerful melodies are led by Gabe, lead guitar, and Tanvi, lead vocals. Felix, Rhythm guitar and vocals, provides a good foundation for the songs’ clean and dynamic rhythms along with drummer Declan. The last addition to the group was Bassist Joey, rounding out the group's deep and grounded sound. Songwriting has maintained to be a collaborative effort for the band. Claiming lots of influence from 2000’s era indie bands, Hallway takes the powerful essence of Indie Rock and balances it with the cool and warm tone of a female fronted rock group.  On May 19th, 2023, Hallway released their first single to the public, ‘Rookie / Metal’.  On October 6th, 2023, Hallway released their second single, ‘Last Time’. Their EP “Codas” is out as of April 24th, 2026. @hallwaytheband Hallway on  Spotify

(cash or venmo accepted at the door) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.

events.title: "Inimigos do fim!" - Tipton-Tsiganov-Lockwood-Barata Quartet
events.description:
$15 admission / 6pm doors / 6:30 show / seated / all ages "Inimigos do Fim!" will feature Brazilian jazz & samba, original jazz tunes, and standards played by a dynamic quartet, including Mark Tipton (trumpet), Alexei Tsiganov (piano & vibes), John Lockwood (bass), and Rafael Barata (drums). "Inimigos do Fim!" translates from Portuguese as "Enemies of the end!," and conveys a spirit of resilience and a passion for life - of refusing to give up! This spirit is at the core of the Tipton-Tsiganov-Lockwood-Barata Quartet's music. 
 
 
 
 Double-click to edit... 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Mark Tipton  
 
 
 Tipton is a Boston-based jazz trumpeter, composer, and educator who has also lived and worked in New York City, Los Angeles, and Portland, Maine. Mark serves as Assistant Chair of Jazz Studies at NEC, where he earned his Doctor of Musical Arts degree. He is an in-demand freelance jazz trumpeter and session musician on the East Coast, and has premiered his compositions throughout the US. His recent albums include Vernacular Stretch (Mark Tipton Jazz Octet plus vocalists; premiered in 2025 in Brooklyn) and Nosferatu Funk (Nondualism Trio; currently in post-production). He also leads the Mark Tipton Jazz Orchestra (big band), and the multi-genre ensemble Les Sorciers Perdus, which specializes in performing his numerous original silent film scores.  Mark is a Faculty member at Samba Meets Jazz, working with Artistic Director Nilson Matta each summer in Bar Harbor, Maine. Mark has recently performed and/or recorded with Jerry Bergonzi, Allan Chase, Diego Figueiredo, Edsel Gomez, Dave Holland, Joe Hunt, Ayn Inserto, Brian Lynch, Nilson Matta, Jason Moran, New England Jazz Collaborative, Chico Pinheiro, Ada Rovatti, Antonio Sanchez, Bert Seager, and Tom Varner. He has recently toured Turkey, Cypress, and the Northeastern US with Mehmet Ali Sanlıkol, and has performed at many venues throughout the US, including Alice Tully Hall, Carnegie Hall, Dizzy’s, Highline Ballroom, Joe’s Pub, NuBlu, and Soapbox Gallery (NYC), The Regattabar, Jordan Hall, Harvard Memorial Chapel, and The Lilypad (Boston, MA), the Beverly Hills Civic Center, Getty Center, Hotel Café, and World Stage (Los Angeles, CA), Sharp 9 Gallery (Durham, NC), and at venues in Europe. Mark has studied privately with John McNeil, Jason Palmer, Jerry Bergonzi, Billy Hart, and Joe Morris. www.marktiptonmusic.com 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Alexei Tsiganov  
 
 
 Tsiganov is a composer, pianist, vibraphonist and educator. His powerful playing and emotionally rich composition style have been captivating jazz lovers all over the world. In the past few years Tsiganov has performed and toured solo and with his group throughout the United States, Europe, South America and Asia.  He has played and recorded with: Claudio Roditi, Antonio Sanchez, Chico Freeman, Esperanza Spalding, Bobby Watson, Victor Lewis, Gene Jackson, Chico Pinheiro, Brian Lynch, Alex Sipiagin, Boris Kozlov, Tony Malaby, Avery Sharp, Jerry Bergonzi, George Garzone, Bob Moses, John Lockwood, Donny McCaslin, Greg Osby, David Kikoski and many others. He has appeared with his group on WERS-Boston radio station and in Eric In the Evening program on WGBH-Boston, performing original music and standards.He studied with Gary Burton at Berklee College of Music, and at the New England Conservatory of Music with Charlie Banacos and George Russell.   alexeitsiganov.com 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 John Lockwood 
 
 
 Lockwood is an internationally renowned acoustic and electric bassist who has toured the U.S. and Europe with Joe Henderson, Freddie Hubbard, Gary Burton, the Mel Lewis Big Band, and The Fringe. He has also performed with the Buffalo Philharmonic, the Boston Pops, MIT Symphony, Pat Metheny, Dizzy Gillespie, Woody Shaw, Toots Thielemans, Stan Getz, and Art Farmer. A Berklee graduate, he studied with Bill Curtis, Henry Portnoi, and Arthur Webb, and currently teaches at NEC and Berklee. necmusic.edu/faculty/john-lockwood 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Rafael Barata 
 
 
 Barata was born in Rio de Janiero, Brazil, began drumming at age 5, and began his studio career at age 14. He has performed and recorded with many legendary musicians, including: Herbie Hancock, Esperanza Spaulding, Milton Nascimento, João Donato, Hermeto Pascoal, Mike Stern, Dianne Reeves, Karrin Allyson, and many others. He has taught masterclasses globally, from Berklee College of Music to USC, Brown University, Sibelius Academy, Escola de música de Brasilia, Escola de música Villa Lobos, and others. Since early 2000s he has been touring around the world, performing at major Jazz festivals and Theaters with these main projects: The "Cello Samba Trio" (with Jaques Morelenbaum and Lula Galvão), spreading the Bossa Nova culture, the Grammy winner Eliane Elias (including, Marc Johnson and Rubens De La Corte) and lately with the multi Grammy winner, Dianne Reeves. You can also find Rafael at Dave Zinno’s quintet Unisphere besides top players such as Mike Tucker, Benny Bloom and Leo Genovese and at his new group, i Trio, with André Vasconcellos on bass and Eduardo Farias on piano. He is also a Multi-Nominated Grammy Winning Drummer, Eliane’s “Made in Brazil” and several nominations including the Brazilian legend, composer, piano player, arranger, publisher and educator, Antonio Adolfo. He also created the "Core of Research and Development of Art and Music", which is a project designed to help with the internal issues that every musician carries emotionally, and how this can affect their music in the end. www.rafaelbarata.com

events.description:

 Double-click to edit... 
 
 
 
 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Continuing Every Monday at 8:30pm Lineup subject to change

 The Fringe  originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist  George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. events.description:
$15 suggested / $5 with Student ID / 6:30pm start / seated 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Bert Seager’s Heart of Hearing is a-jazz quartet made up of piano, tenor-saxophone, upright-bass, and drums whose aim is to bring listeners into the heart of improvised jazz. The joyful expression of this musical intimacy, the shimmering transparency of the sound, and the sense that these musicians are as much involved in listening as in playing makes for compelling and memorable performances.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Bert Seager , pianist, composer, recording artist, and educator, has led performances in international jazz festivals in Canada, Peru, Bulgaria, Jordan, Ecuador, Israel, China and Japan. As a composer, he is a three-time recipient of the prestigious MacDowell Colony fellowship, an artists residency program in Peterborough, New Hampshire. He has recorded 18 compact discs which have all been released internationally to critical acclaim. Cadence Magazine says Bert’s music is filled with “effervescent optimism.” And the Boston Globe wrote that his “kind of exuberance makes the jazz world go round.” 
 Rick DiMuzio , tenor saxophonist, composer, and educator, has performed concerts and clinics throughout the United States, Europe, Central and South America, and Asia. In addition to his performing career, Rick is a full Professor at Berklee College of Music where he teaches ear training, improvisation, saxophone, and ensembles. He earned his doctorate in jazz composition from New England Conservatory, a master’s degree in jazz performance from the Eastman School of Music, and a bachelor’s degree in music education from Indiana University of PA.  
 Bassist  Andrew Schiller , after living in Brooklyn NY, for five years, working as a bandleader and sideman playing jazz and improvised music, came to Boston to earn his doctorate in music from the New England Conservatory in 2020. He is now teaching at Berklee College of Music and Salem State University. Andrew’s debut album, "Tied Together, Not To The Ground," was released in May 2017, and his most recent project is "Sonoran," an 9-part suite for quintet are both on Red Piano Records. These albums feature an adventurous and unique compositional style, blending jazz with contemporary classical, rock, and avant-garde influences. 
 Dor Herskovits  is an Israeli drummer and composer based in Boston. Following his passion for jazz and improvised music, Herskovits received his Bachelor’s degree from the Berklee College of music and his Master’s degree in Jazz Performance from the New England Conservatory. During these formative years, the drummer also began his journey as a composer and bandleader. Today, Herskovits performs and records as a sideman and a bandleader around the world. His current projects include – Earprint, Tetraptych, Bert Seager, Elan Mehler trio, TJ and the Revenge, Max Ridley’s Basement Orchestra, Xiongguan Zhang, and many others. He has shared the stage with great musicians such as Jason Palmer, Steve Cardenas, Jon Cowherd, Daniel Rotem and George Garzone. 
 
 
 bertseager.com

 Inspired by the cartoon music of the 50s and 60s, the drive of Led Zeppelin, the genius and humor of Frank Zappa, the perfection of Bach, the relentlessness of Ligeti, the courage of Medeski, Martin and Wood, the jam of Phish live, the beauty of the Beatles and the immersive nature of music, I am in pursuit of truth through music. “Sometimes I think of us musicians as kids playing in order to learn how to be adults, but we can just keep playing.  Joe Hunt  is a jazz drummer, educator, author, and historian. In the early 1960s, Joe Hunt performed and recorded alongside the late NEC Distinguished Artist-in-Residence Emeritus George Russell, with releases on Decca and Riverside. Hunt joined The Stan Getz Quartet in 1964, recording several releases on Verve, then was a member of the Bill Evans Trio from 1966-1967. The remainder of the 1960s found Hunt performing or recording with several other jazz luminaries including Chet Baker, Eric Dolphy, Dizzy Gillespie, Dexter Gordon, Charles Mingus, Bob Brookmeyer, and the late Herb Pomeroy. In the 1970s and 1980s, Hunt was a member of The National Jazz Ensemble, led jazz groups with John Scofield, Mike Stern, and Santi Debriano, and toured with quartets of Red Rodney and Hal McKusick. The 1990s, and beyond, have included membership in The Smithsonian Jazz Masters Orchestra, with former NEC president Gunther Schuller, performances with Kenny Burrell, Joe Lavano, Joanne Brackeen, and Tal Farlow, as well as recordings with the Bert Seager Quintet, and also, Trio. Hunt is the author of the 1994 book 52nd Street Beat, which is a historical look at jazz drummer greats from 1945 to 1965. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Joe Hunt quartet features a modern jazz ensemble music played by top local pros: Mark Pinto - alto saxophone, formerly years with the Buddy Rich band John Lockwood – bass, formerly with Joe Henderson, Lee Konitz, current Fringe member Yuka Hamano Hunt – piano, voice, arranger Joe Hunt – drums, formerly with George Russell, Stan Getz, Jim Hall, Dexter Gordon, and Bill Evans We pay tribute to a special composer or performer at most performances. Recent shows have included: Burt Bacharach, Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Gigi Gryce. Future shows will include the music of Paul and Carla Bley, and arranger, Johnny Mandel. - Continuing of the 3rd Sunday of Every Month

 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer.  A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

events.title: Barabas - Orbit | Album Launch Concert
events.description:
$22 admission / 7:15 doors / 7:30 show / seated & standing 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Orbit  is the new solo album by Hungarian trumpeter, pianist, and composer  Lőrinc Barabás , who now performs his solo project under the name  Barabas . The album is a cinematic and meditative musical journey where neoclassical piano, ambient soundscapes, and electronic textures come together. The ten compositions explore the ideas of movement and cycles. As the world around us moves ever faster, the music invites listeners to slow down, turn inward, and discover moments of stillness. Trumpet, piano, and synthesizers engage in a musical dialogue, creating a sound world that is both intimate and expansive, moving between ambient, neoclassical, and electronic music. Throughout his nearly two-decade career,  Lőrinc Barabás has released thirteen albums , performed regularly across Europe and the United States, and collaborated with artists including  Erik Truffaz, Takuya Kuroda, Niklas Paschburg, and Valerie June . His international appearances include the  EFG London Jazz Festival at the Barbican , the  Jazzycolors Festival in Paris ,  The Town Hall in New York City ,  Expo 2020 Dubai , and  Expo 2025 Osaka . The album launch concert at  The Lilypad in Cambridge, just outside Boston , brings the world of  Orbit  to life on stage, where acoustic instruments and electronics merge into one continuous, immersive musical experience. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Barabas  
 
 
 Barabas is the solo project of Hungarian trumpeter and composer Lőrinc Barabás. Blending trumpet, piano, synthesizers, and electronics, his music moves between neoclassical, ambient, contemporary jazz, and electronic music, creating a cinematic sound world built around strong melodies, improvisation, and atmospheric textures. Over a career spanning nearly two decades, Barabás has released twelve albums across solo and ensemble projects. His solo catalogue includes Sastra (2013), Elevator Dance Music (2015), Algorhythms (2019), and the intimate, piano-centered 22 (2023). His latest album, Orbit (2026), develops this musical language further, bringing minimalist piano, atmospheric synthesizers, electronic rhythms, and trumpet into a more spacious and meditative setting. As a live artist, Barabas transforms this material into an immersive solo performance, moving fluidly between piano, trumpet, synthesizers, looping, and electronics. Rather than separating acoustic and electronic music, he uses them as parts of the same musical language, allowing composed pieces and improvisation to evolve naturally on stage. Barabás has toured extensively throughout Europe and the United States, opened for Jean-Michel Jarre, and collaborated with artists including Erik Truffaz, Takuya Kuroda, Niklas Paschburg, and Valerie June. International appearances include the EFG London Jazz Festival at the Barbican, Brooklyn Public Library, The Town Hall in New York, Expo 2020 Dubai, and Expo 2025 Osaka. Performing his solo project under the name Barabas, he brings together nearly two decades of musical exploration in a distinctive contemporary identity — trumpet, piano, and electronics meeting somewhere between the concert hall, jazz club, and electronic stage.

 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. events.title: Orkest
events.description:
Founded in 2022 by Sapphire Skye Toth and Michael Gehman while they earned their Master of Science degrees in Arts Administration at Boston University, Orkest is meant to be the place where New Music meets The Community and The Community meets New Music.

Orkest, a visionary musical venture rooted in the bustling city of Boston, is on a mission to redefine the local music scene. Recognizing the abundance of untapped musical talent, Orkest seeks to bridge the gap between emerging composers and the community, breaking away from classical traditions and creating an inviting space for diverse genres. Departing from conventional models, Orkest utilizes venues to bring people to music, not just vice versa, fostering a casual environment in cafe bars and libraries. With a commitment to equitable treatment of artists, creating opportunities for artists at socioeconomic disadvantages, professional recordings of performances, and a unique pay-what-you-wish model, Orkest is not just a music experience; it's a transformative force shaping how communities engage with and appreciate new music and the artists who create it.

Pandji Pragiwaksono
 is an Indonesian stand-up comedian and entertainment innovator who dominated his home country's comedy scene before taking on the global stage. His 2025 special Mens Rea became the biggest comedy special in Indonesian history, sparking thousands of protests and direct government response. After reaching the pinnacle of success in Indonesia, Pandji made the bold decision to start his career anew, pursuing success in English. His first English-language comedy special, "Boss Level," debuted in 2026 and launched his international career. Now touring the world, Pandji performs in both English and Indonesian, bringing his fearless storytelling to audiences globally. Over two decades, Pandji has built a multifaceted career as a radio broadcaster, television presenter, comic publisher, and musician. He co-founded KolamKomik.com and released the rap album Provocative Proactive in 2008. From radio to comedy stages to comics and hip-hop, Pandji has proven himself a versatile force in entertainment. Now conquering the international stage, he's demonstrating that true artistry transcends language and borders.

Maison Électronique is an instrumental trio playing original 
compositions that blend Congolese rumba and contemporary seben guitar 
styles with other African musics and Western styles like shoegaze, surf,
 and dub. The group is led by guitarist Nathaniel Braddock. Braddock has

Ellen Sugarman
's comedy has been called both accessible and unique. events.title: JAZZ NIGHT: Bill Jones Trio
events.description: Bill Jones, a native of Marion, Massachusetts, is a tenor and soprano saxophonist that been a regular on the jazz scene since he moved to Boston in 1999 to study at the New England Conservatory. He is inspired by such greats as Joe Henderson, John Coltrane, Hank Mobley, Wayne Shorter, and Charlie Parker, as well as modern masters like Jerry Bergonzi, George Garzone, Joe Lovano, Joshua Redman, and Mark Turner. Bill regularly plays at venues in and around Boston, such as Wally’s, The Beehive, Monkfish, and Lilypad. He enjoys playing classic and modern jazz standards and his original compositions. He has performed with many revered jazz musicians, such as Bob Gullotti, Leo Genovese, Herb Pomeroy, Jeff Galindo, Tim Ray, Greg Hopkins, and John Lockwood.

events.title: The Space Consortium's Space Table
events.description:
Whether you're a space professional, student, educator, science communicator, longtime space enthusiast, or simply curious about space, come enjoy an informal evening of conversation, games, and new connections.

The Space Table is our new monthly gathering bringing together Space Consortium Members (MA-based space academics and professionals) and Explorers (space enthusiasts) for space and science conversations, board games, discussions, and more. What happens at The Space Table will be shaped by you: share what you're working on, pick a space or science topic to discuss, join a game, meet someone with completely different expertise, and tell us what you'd like to see at future gatherings.

No space background or expertise is required. Everyone is welcome!
Free and open to all: Registration is free, but spots are limited, so register now to reserve yours.

Liam Nelson
 is a New York City-based comedian hailing from Atlanta, Georgia. Standing an impressive 7 feet tall and living with Marfan Syndrome, Liam offers a unique perspective on life as a "walking spectacle." At just 26 years old, he weaves sharp, hilarious commentary on navigating the world as a disabled young adult with stories that are equal parts outrageous and deeply relatable. He’s headlined nationwide along with performing with top comics like Sam Morril, Gianmarco Soresi and Dusty Slay, appeared at the Netflix Is A Joke festival, and released his first Dry Bar Comedy Special in 2025. He also appeared on the 2026 season of Netflix’s Star Search Reboot.

events.title: JAZZ NIGHT: Dave Fox Trio
events.description:
The Dave Fox Trio is a Modern Jazz Trio featuring original jazz
compositions and arrangements inspired by artists such as John Coltrane, Joe Henderson, Chick Corea, Steve Swallow, Charles Mingus, Thelonious Monk and Wayne Shorter. The group features internationally acclaimed bassist John Lockwood and innovative Boston area musicians and composers such as guitarist Phil Sargent and saxophonists Nicholas Brust and Bill Jones.

Dave Fox is an accomplished, versatile drummer and is currently a full-time member of The Gravel Project, Dan Rockett and The Guilty Party and
“AS3” along with Andrew Stern and Brad Barrett.

As a sideman for over two decades, he has performed with a diverse group of artists including Jerry Bergonzi, John Lockwood, Josh Smith, Dave Tronzo, Charles Neville, Stan Strickland, The Stompers and Tom Hambridge and The Rattlesnakes to name a few.

events.title: Ricky Stein
events.description: Austin-born singer/songwriter Ricky Stein writes songs that seek to find spiritual common ground between the mesas of West Texas and the streetscapes of the world's great music capitals. Original compositions such as "Night Shines On," "American Dreaming," and "The Great Empty" capture the energy of urban life in the modern era; latest single "Heart of the Night" seeks hope and meaning through human connection. All songs are delivered in an earnest baritone accompanied by acoustic guitar, harmonica, and a good-humored stage presence.
